Abbadie1860.method: Printed Latin rendering of Ethiopic V.2.ii, printed116/physical128. Mediated versional evidence, not direct Geʿez or a separate Latin codex family.

excerpts.finding: All eight paragraphs are on physical317/printed301. Physical318 begins V.2.iii, although the canonical page map lists both. The text retains fifteen days, fasting and prayer; offspring’s God-rejection, Lord-blasphemy, betrayal without gain and filled-up lawlessness; wife/future sister and mercy; disclosure and forgiveness for the family and all holy ones, conditional on whole-hearted repentance AND removal of double-mindedness; the appointed-day/no-salvation warning, righteous/holy-ones limits and nations until the final day; church leaders and full promises; perseverance, no double-mindedness, passage with holy angels, tribulation and NOT denying their life; the Son oath, Lord-denial, now-future deniers and mercy already shown to prior deniers. The printed verb in8 is ἀπεγνωρίσθαι; only the imported omission of ρι is corrected.

All eight paragraphs of the diplomatic transcription were read at3000px. God and Lord are distinct in2. The collective seed initially has singular rejection/blasphemy forms; no gain is retained, but the separate closing filled-up-lawlessness clause is absent. Wife/future sister and mercy remain. Paragraph4 retains whole-heart repentance and double-mindedness removal and has an explicit future forgiveness clause for the holy ones. Paragraph5 retains the deadline/no-salvation warning and distinct groups. Paragraph6 retains leaders and promises. Paragraph7 has your passage with holy angels and the negative οὐκ before denying their life. Paragraph8 has Lord and ἀπεγνωρίσθαι, lacks the working νῦν before future denial, and retains prior-deniers past mercy. This is the same Athos codex as in other editions, not a separate edition vote or fresh photograph collation.

All eight explicit ab elements and their app/rdg layers were read; none contains a gap or supplied element. Paragraphs1–2 retain the fifteen-day setting, God/Lord distinction, no gain and filled-up lawlessness. In3 ca adds your before sister; the final mercy verb is transcribed exeis rather than working exei. In4 first pote is corrected by ca to tote; all holy ones, whole-heart repentance and removal of double-mindedness remain. In5 the warnings and groups remain, with spelling corrections. In6 ca changes the ways pronoun and corrects a dotted promise-word spelling. In7 first our, parados and the difficult life spelling zy are corrected by S1 to your, parodos and zoen; ca changes their to their own. The negative ouk is present without a correction. In8 first XN, Christ, is changed by ca to KN, Lord; the verb retains ri, and now-future denial and prior-deniers past mercy remain. Correctors are not additional codices; no original photographs were collated.

The Vulgata section begins on printed8, continues through9 and ends on10 (physical27–29). Paragraph2 has seed and sin against Lord, lacks the separate blasphemy clause, and prints positive profecerunt, they profited, rather than the Greek no-gain statement. The final fullness clause remains. Paragraph3 retains wife/future sister and mercy. Before the forgiveness transition it adds she will be instructed. In4 printed mihi, me, is an editorial emendation against reported him forms; the main text has the all-saints clause, with omission reported for D and Vat. Whole-heart repentance and doubt removal remain. Paragraph5 retains the deadline/no-salvation warning and group limits;6 has leaders and full promise. Paragraph7 lacks the separate do-not-be-double-minded prohibition but retains the negative about denying their life. Paragraph8 has the Son oath and the Son as denied object, future deniers and past mercy; printed unquam, ever, is an emendation against reported nunquam, never. These printed emendations are not preserved codex readings.

Palatina paragraphs1–4 begin on printed19,4–8 continue on21, and8 ends on23 (physical116/118/120). Seed, both Lord clauses, parent betrayal without benefit and filled-up lawlessness remain. The wife begins to be a sister and receives mercy. Paragraph4 has all who sinned without the holy-ones label here, with whole-heart repentance and doubt removal. Paragraph5 retains the deadline/no-salvation warning and limits for the different groups. Paragraph6 has leaders and full promise. Paragraph7 retains the negative about denying their life; its perseverate and nolite are editorial emendations of reported forms. Paragraph8 has the Son oath, Lord-denial and future propitiabitur for mercy to earlier deniers. That future is not silently treated as the working past tense.

The Latin rendering of Ethiopic V.2.ii is entirely on printed116/physical128; physical129 is the next section. Paragraph2 has no separate seed word in its main text; the footnote proposes a change to agree with Greek and Latin. It has Lord in both offenses, parent betrayal without profit, added sins, and no separate closing fullness clause. Paragraph3 has the difficult futurae tuae phrase, tongue restraint and mercy. Paragraph4 has all who sinned without the holy-ones label here, whole-heart repentance and leaving doubt. Paragraph5 has they will not live for the appointed-limit warning and retains the group limits. Paragraph6 has leaders and full hope/glory. Paragraph7 has return with holy angels and endurance, but POSITIVE denial of their life. Paragraph8 has the Son oath, Lord-denial, future deniers and future condonabit for mercy to prior deniers. This is comparison through the printed Latin rendering, not direct Geʿez collation or reconstructed Greek.

Bodmer38 metadata reports Visions coverage, but no passage image or edition transcription has been acquired; metadata supplies neither corroboration nor an absence vote. Michigan129 does not cover the Visions. Other extant versions/excerpts and original manuscript photographs remain uncollated.
